Module np.cincuentazo
Package np.cincuentazo.controller

Class SceneNavigator

java.lang.Object
np.cincuentazo.controller.SceneNavigator
public final class SceneNavigator extends Object
Centralises all scene-navigation logic for the Cincuentazo application.

Before this class existed, every controller loaded FXML, created a Scene, obtained the Stage from a node, called Stage.setScene(Scene) and Stage.setTitle(String) inline â€” the same five-line boilerplate repeated in four different places. SceneNavigator extracts that boilerplate into one place and exposes three semantic, destination-specific methods so callers read as plain intent.

Design decisions

  • Final / utility class: all methods are static and the constructor is private. There is nothing to instantiate â€” the class is a collection of pure functions that transform a JavaFX scene graph.
  • Stage obtained from a Node: controllers do not hold a direct reference to the stage. Instead, any node currently attached to the scene graph can reach the stage via node.getScene().getWindow(). This keeps controllers stage-agnostic and easy to test.
  • Unchecked wrapping: IOException from FXMLLoader is wrapped in RuntimeException. Navigation failures are programming errors (wrong FXML path), not recoverable user-facing conditions, so forcing every call site to handle a checked exception would be noise.
  • Single package: placed alongside the controllers that use it (np.cincuentazo.controller) so no new package declaration is needed in module-info.java.

SRP

This class has exactly one reason to change: the mechanics of how the application switches between its three screens. If a fourth screen is ever added, only this class and its callers change â€” not the navigation logic scattered across every controller.

      public static void toStartScreen(javafx.scene.Node anyNode)
      Navigates to the start / configuration screen (start-view.fxml).

      Used by:

      • GameController.onNewGame() â€” player wants a fresh game.
      • VictoryController.onStart() â€” player wants to change the number of machine opponents.
      Parameters:
      anyNode - any node currently attached to the scene whose Stage will host the new scene; must not be null and must already be part of an active scene

    • toGameScreen

      public static void toGameScreen(javafx.scene.Node anyNode, int numMachines)
      Navigates to the main game screen (game-view.fxml) and immediately starts a game with the given number of machine players.

      Calls GameController.startGame(int) on the newly created controller before making the scene visible, so the game is fully initialised the moment the player sees the board.

      Used by:

      • StartController.onStart() â€” first game of a session.
      • VictoryController.onPlayAgain() â€” rematch with same config.
      Parameters:
      anyNode - any node currently attached to the scene whose Stage will host the new scene
      numMachines - number of machine opponents to include (1â€“3)
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if game-view.fxml cannot be loaded

    • toVictoryScreen

      public static void toVictoryScreen(javafx.scene.Node anyNode, boolean humanWon, String winnerName, int numberOfMachines)
      Navigates to the victory / results screen (victory-view.fxml) and injects the game result into the controller.

      Calls VictoryController.setResult(boolean, String, int) on the newly created controller before the scene becomes visible.

      Used by GameController.navigateToVictoryScreen() when the game detects that only one player remains (HU-6).

      Parameters:
      anyNode - any node currently attached to the scene whose Stage will host the new scene
      humanWon - true if the human player is the sole survivor
      winnerName - display name of the winning player
      numberOfMachines - number of machine opponents in the finished game
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if victory-view.fxml cannot be loaded
